knowledge_point.title: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cotangent Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we just take the constant out of the derivative and use the result for the derivative of $\operatorname{cot}x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{'}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-1\operatorname{cot}x) \\  & =-1(-\csc^{2}x) \\  & =1\csc^{2}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{'}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =1\csc^{2}(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =1{(2)}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
